step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Analyzed the visual whiteboard architecture and audio transcript for the Singapore Exchange (SGX) Investor Portal.
2. Identified all active runtime components and matched them to the strict valid vocabulary list:
   - USERS -> UserConsumerWeb
   - CLOUDFRONT -> CloudFront
   - WAF -> WAF
   - LAMBDA@EDGE -> LambdaAtEdge
   - S3 -> S3
   - API GW -> ApiGateway
   - LAMBDA -> Lambda
   - ELASTICACHE -> ElastiCache
   - ELB -> ELB
   - EC2 -> EC2
   - DX -> DirectConnect
   - DC -> OnPremDC
3. Mapped the flows into two distinct logical workflows:
   - Flow 0: Frontend Single Page Application delivery (CloudFront, WAF, Lambda@Edge, S3 to USERS).
   - Flow 1: Backend API authentication and hybrid microservice request processing (USERS -> API GW -> Lambda authorizer -> ElastiCache -> ELB -> EC2 -> DirectConnect -> DC).

graph.name: Singapore Exchange Investor Portal Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture for SGX's investor portal using AWS CloudFront, Lambda@Edge, API Gateway, Lambda authorizer, ElastiCache, EC2, and Direct Connect for hybrid integration with the on-premises data center.

nodes.name: USERS
nodes.notes: Retail investors accessing the SGX investor portal web application.

nodes.name: CLOUDFRONT
nodes.notes: AWS CloudFront CDN serving static frontend artifacts.

nodes.name: WAF
nodes.notes: AWS WAF protecting CloudFront with security rules and IP filtering.

nodes.name: LAMBDA@EDGE
nodes.notes: Lambda@Edge for edge compute, custom routing, and security headers.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Amazon S3 storing static web assets, encrypted with KMS.

nodes.name: API GW
nodes.notes: Amazon API Gateway serving as the backend entry point with mutual TLS / client certs.

nodes.name: LAMBDA
nodes.notes: Lambda authorizer executing step zero authentication checks.

nodes.name: ELASTICACHE
nodes.notes: Amazon ElastiCache for storing and validating active session state.

nodes.name: ELB
nodes.notes: Elastic Load Balancing distributing authenticated API requests to backend EC2 services.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Amazon EC2 hosting microservices that manage user sessions and business logic.

nodes.name: DX
nodes.notes: AWS Direct Connect providing dedicated connectivity between AWS VPC and on-premises DC.

nodes.name: DC
nodes.notes: On-premises Data Center hosting legacy exchange core backends and databases.

edges.notes: WAF filters and protects traffic entering CloudFront.
CloudFront serves static single page application assets back to the user's web browser.
CloudFront triggers Lambda@Edge for edge routing and inserting security headers.
CloudFront retrieves web artifacts from S3.
User browser sends session and API requests to API Gateway.
API Gateway invokes Lambda authorizer as step zero authentication.
Lambda authorizer checks session state in ElastiCache.
API Gateway forwards authenticated requests to ELB.
ELB routes API requests to backend microservices on EC2.
EC2 microservices read and write session data in ElastiCache.
Direct Connect links AWS backend services to the on-premises Data Center.
